name: fundrail
description: ETF operations console: nightly fund files → filings, Rule 6c-11 disclosures, compliance tests, and a tamper-evident evidence chain. A Next.js/TypeScript demo over a fictional 90-fund trust.

paragraphs: An ETF operations console: one morning at a 90-fund trust, run as software.

Every night, a fund issuer's outside accountants send it files saying what each fund owns and what it's worth. Every morning, before the market opens, the issuer owes the world regulated outputs built from those files: a refreshed public page per fund, portfolio filings for the SEC, tax and naming tests, and receipts for all of it. fundrail plays out that 7:00am cycle over a fictional 90-fund trust: it catches the problems hiding in the files, blocks what must not ship, publishes what can, and records every action in a tamper-evident log.

The work scales with the fund count, but the deadline never moves: every trading day, before open. And the failure modes are public. A stale number on a fund's website is a rule violation the SEC has cited real issuers for; a bad value in a filing is worse. When examiners arrive, "who approved this and when" has to be answerable in minutes, not reconstructed from email archaeology.
features: The N-PORT output is a small Part C subset, not an EDGAR-accepted submission, and it says so in every artifact.
IRC 851 covers the core 25% and 50% asset-diversification tests; the finer prongs are out of scope.
The 30-day median bid-ask spread is a fixed sample, not computed from live quote data.
Evidence fingerprints are FNV-1a-32 so they stay readable; production would use SHA-256 in append-only storage.
All funds, tickers, and numbers are fictional.
